Optimal.Notes: A slight bump to medium textures and 1024x640 render resolution gives noticeably better image quality over MaxBattery with manageable power draw. Towns will still see occasional dips to ~25 fps; the 40 Hz refresh rate makes 30 fps feel smoother.

profiles.Summary: Dragon's Dogma 2 is a demanding RE Engine action-RPG that significantly exceeds the Steam Deck's GPU capabilities, requiring heavy compromises in settings and resolution to approach a playable 30 fps. With FSR upscaling and low settings it can reach a rough 30 fps in open areas, but crowded towns and dense combat scenes will cause noticeable drops.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum requirements (GTX 1660 / RX 5500 XT target) versus Deck GPU capability (~GTX 1050 Ti class) and general RE Engine behaviour. On your first run, check frame rate in Vernworth (the main city) — that is the worst-case scenario — and drop to MaxBattery settings or a 25 fps cap if it is unacceptably choppy.

MaxBattery.Notes: Use in-game FSR 2 upscaler set to Performance mode alongside the Deck's FSR overlay for the best battery savings; towns will still dip below 30 fps occasionally.

KnownIssues: No native Linux build; runs via Proton with silver/gold ProtonDB tier — some players report crashes or instability
Frame rate drops significantly in cities like Vernworth due to NPC crowd simulation CPU load
Ray tracing is unsupported on Deck-class hardware and must be disabled
Denuvo DRM and online requirement at launch may cause additional overhead or connectivity prompts

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full 15 W TDP with GPU at max clock targets a 40 fps cap in open world and combat; expect drops to 28-33 fps in dense city areas. Battery life is short — best suited for docked or plugged-in play near a charger.

Optimal.Notes: A step up in shadow and mesh fidelity over MaxBattery while still targeting 30 fps; the higher GPU clock helps maintain the cap in open-world areas. Busy city streets will still cause dips — this is a known engine limitation even on strong PCs.

profiles.Summary: Dragon's Dogma 2 is a demanding RE Engine title whose PC minimum GPU (GTX 1660 / RX 5500 XT 8 GB) already exceeds the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU by a significant margin, making smooth play a real challenge. Expect 30 fps to be the realistic ceiling at low/medium settings with FSR upscaling, and frame drops in dense urban areas or large enemy encounters.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1660 / RX 5500 XT, well above Deck GPU class) and RE Engine behaviour on similar hardware. On your first run, check frame rate in a city area — if it stays below 25 fps consistently, drop to MaxBattery settings or lower render resolution further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and let Deck FSR upscale to 1280x800; the 8 W TDP and locked GPU clock reduce heat and fan noise considerably. Expect dips below 30 in cities — consider dropping to Vernworth interiors or fast-travelling to reduce load.

KnownIssues: No native Linux build; runs via Proton — some users report crashes or instability on launch requiring Proton version tweaks.
Frame rate drops significantly in cities (Vernworth) and during large multi-enemy encounters even on capable PCs, so Deck performance will be notably worse in these areas.
Denuvo DRM may cause additional CPU overhead and occasional stutters, especially on first-run shader compilation.
HDR output may not initialise correctly under Proton; disabling in-game HDR and using the Deck's native display mode is recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full 1280x800 native with medium settings is the visual ceiling the Deck can attempt, but expect frequent dips to the mid-20s in Vernworth and complex fights; reduce Shadow Quality to Low if stuttering is persistent. Battery life will be short at full TDP.
